note: Hand-derived from reducer.ExtractSymbolRuntimeIntentRows's real extraction path over symbol_runtime_family_odu.go's fixture, filtered to the runs_in domain's upsert rows, fanned out against reducer.ExtractWorkloadCandidates -> reducer.BuildProjectionRows's WorkloadRows for the same repository. This fixture proves LIVE that the family is not merely a one-edge assertion that cannot distinguish 'processed every route-bound function' from 'processed only the first one': HandleWidgets (GET+POST /widgets, deduped to one row by runs_in's own functionID+repoID dedupe key, which has no method dimension) and HandleHealth (GET /healthz, a distinct handler on a distinct path) both bind, yielding TWO edges. A regression that stopped after the first resolved handler would silently drop the HandleHealth edge, and this exact-set assertion would catch it as MISSING by name. The repository DEFINES exactly one Workload here, so the fan-out this fixture exercises per-row is still 1-row-to-1-edge (2 rows, 2 edges, not a cross product). The live Cypher's (Repository)-[:DEFINES]->(Workload) MATCH carries no LIMIT, so the WRITE TEMPLATE would permit an N-Workload fan-out -- but today's reducer.ExtractWorkloadCandidates/BuildProjectionRows cap a single repository at exactly one Workload (workload signals aggregate per repo_id, and one WorkloadRow is emitted per candidate), so no live fixture can currently exhibit two Workloads for one repository to prove that direction end to end. The general N-Workload cross product this guard would still compute correctly if the projection ever contained one is proven deterministically by a synthetic offline unit test instead (materialized_edges_runs_in_test.go), not by adding a second Workload to this live fixture, per the coordinator's explicit instruction that the honest single-workload case is sufficient here. source_entity_id is each handler's canonical Function uid (content.CanonicalEntityID) -- the same function_id HANDLES_ROUTE resolves for the same handler, since runs_in reuses the identical handlesRouteEntries route data. target_entity_id is the deterministic (non-hashed) workload id BuildProjectionRows derives: "workload:" + the repository's Name field (WorkloadName is never set in this fixture, so it falls back to RepoName) -- the SAME workload id for both edges, since both handlers belong to the one repository/one Workload.
